extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant reviewers and research teams developing R21/R33 preclinical microbicide projects
extracted.subtask_description: Preclinical R21→R33 research plan and selection/evaluation criteria for SEVI-binding microbicide candidates, including assay endpoints, progression/milestone thresholds, human subjects and animal testing requirements, biosafety, and statistical analysis plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progression criteria to specialized R33 assays
rubrics_metrics.description: Compounds will be selected for progression to specialized assays (Aims 3A3 and beyond) if their TI is > 100 (non-colored compounds) or > 500 (colored compounds) and if they show sub-micromolar activity against semen-mediated enhancement of virus infection in CEM-M7 cells and PBMC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because specialized assays are time- and resource-intensive, no more than 3-4 compounds will be progressed per year based on relative ranking of TI values and IC50 in primary cell-based assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 milestone #1: binding affinity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical synthesis of >1 molecule(s) with submicromolar affinity for SEVI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: BTA-EG6 binding affinity for SEVI is 8 µM; this affinity is suboptimal and must be improved to enter R33 with a high likelihood of achieving clinically useful efficacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 milestone #2: therapeutic index threshold (R21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of >1 molecule(s) with a therapeutic index (TI) > 50. The TI will be based on: (i) the IC50 for blockade of semen-mediated enhancement of HIV-1 infection in CEM-M7 cells & (ii) the TC50 for A2En cervicovaginal epithelial cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For colored compounds, TI will be > 250. Rationale: A TI of >50 balances need for high potency at R33 versus avoiding prematurely discarding leads early in development.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 milestone #3: primary cell activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of >1 molecule(s) with submicromolar activity in primary cell-based assays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Activity in primary cell based assays (PBMC or A2En/PBMC trans-infection model) is essential for progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 milestone #4: clade panel breadth
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of >1 molecule(s) with submicromolar activity in clade panel testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Activity against diverse HIV-1 strains (clades A, B, C, transmitted virus) is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: R33 milestone #5: combination activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of >1 molecule(s) with additive or synergistic activity in drug combination testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: SEVI-binding molecules are expected to pair well with conventional microbicides having different mechanisms; combinations will be analyzed (additive/synergistic/antagonistic).

rubrics_metrics.name: R33 milestone #6: minimal toxicity in specialized assays
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of >1 molecule(s) with minimal or undetectable toxicity in specialized assays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required lack of toxicity includes: minimal effect on beneficial Lactobacillus species, preservation of epithelial monolayer integrity, and lack of toxicity in human cervical explants. Additionally, toxicity in the RVI model should be below the cutoff score (8) for acceptability in clinical trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: R33 milestone #7: high TI and potency (R33 endpoint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of >1 molecule(s) with TI > 1,000 and activity in the nanomolar range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: A viable lead candidate microbicide must have robust activity for clinical usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for RVI (rabbit vaginal irritation) testing
rubrics_metrics.description: The most promising lead molecule will be selected for RVI testing on the basis of (i) relative ranking of TI and IC50 values, (ii) stability in HEC and biofluids (Aim 3A3), (iii) efficacy in the explant infection model (Aim 3B) and (iv) a lack of toxicity in Aims 4A thru 4C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RVI groups: [1] HEC control, [2-4] HEC + test compound at 3 escalating dose levels representing 5x, 25x and 100x the IC50 from the explant model, [5] N9 gel control. 27 animals total (n=6 per group except N9 group n=3). Outcomes assessed semiquantitatively for epithelial damage, immune cell infiltration, edema and vascular congestion after 14-day intravaginal delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: pH transition assay as functional stability criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Activity in a pH transition assay that mimics pH change when semen (pH ~7.7) mixes with vaginal fluid (pH ~4); compounds incubated appropriately with target cells and semen-treated virus, followed by trans-infection and direct analysis of cell-bound HIV-1 p24 antigen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: low pH exposure is short and effect on cell viability minimal. Expected result: compounds stable and active; if not, modify BTA-EGx framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physicochemical stability in biologically relevant fluids
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess compound stability by HPLC and/or MS in (i) seminal plasma, (ii) simulated vaginal fluid at pH 4, and (iii) HEC. Incubation 0–24 hrs at 37°C with sampling every 2–4 hrs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expected compounds to be stable and active in the pH transition assay; instability will prompt chemical modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cervical explant efficacy testing criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate efficacy in an unstimulated cervical explant (CE) model using ectocervical tissue: test each compound at 4 concentrations with 4 replicates; infection with HIV-1BaL ± SEVI; measure virus replication by HIV-1 Gag p24 ELISA over 14–18 days; determine IC50 at the assay soft endpoint (SOFT); test in tissue from 2 donors; tenofovir as positive control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If SEVI enhancement is not observed, alternatives include polarized/stimulated explants or focusing on other assays (Aims 1,2) and toxicity evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination drug assay design and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-drug combination assays: test 8 concentrations of BTA-EGx in all combinations with 5 concentrations of candidate microbicides; each drug also tested alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data analysis via MacSynergy II to classify interactions as antagonistic, additive, or synergistic; use stavudine + ribavirin as antagonism control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lactobacillus toxicity assay standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess effect on Lactobacillus crispatus and L. jensenii by incubation in MRS broth with test compounds for 24 hrs using 6 half log10 dilutions in triplicate; penicillin-streptomycin as positive toxicity control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expected: no toxicity. If toxicity occurs, test chemical framework modifications or alternative derivatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epithelial monolayer integrity assay standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess integrity of HEC-1-A and Caco-2 cell monolayers grown on transwell supports; add non-toxic dose apically and measure electrical resistance using a MilliCell-ERS system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: N9 used as positive control for disruption, isomolar Universal Placebo (HEC) as negative control; non-toxic dose determination precedes testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explant toxicity and inflammatory markers criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Toxicity to human cervical explants assessed by MTT after 18–24 hr incubation; use 2–4 half log10 dilutions in triplicate and N9 as positive control; repeat using tissue from at least 2 donors. Assess selected pro-inflammatory cytokines/chemokines (IL-1ß, IL-6, TNFα, MCP-1/CCL2, MIP3α/CCL20, IL-8) via Luminex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expected: lack of toxicity and minimal inflammatory cytokine induction; findings guide further modifications or selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparisons between treatment groups generally performed by one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post-test; single comparisons versus control by two-tailed Student's t test; comparisons of >2 factors by two-way ANOVA with Tukey post-test; non-parametric tests (Kruskal-Wallis or Mann-Whitney U) used if data not normally distributed. Significance taken at p<0.05.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All data analyzed in consultation with the biostatistical co-investigator; group sizes for in vivo studies discussed elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on candidate progression per year
rubrics_metrics.description: No more than 3–4 compounds will be progressed per year to specialized assays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection based on relative ranking of TI values and IC50 in primary cell-based assays due to resource intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects inclusion/exclusion and consent protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective semen donors: male volunteers, ages 18–55, HIV-positive individuals and vulnerable populations (children, prisoners, institutionalized) excluded. Consent obtained and documented; HIPAA authorization obtained when PHI collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Samples deidentified and assigned unique code known only to the consent administrator (Ms. Bunce); no PHI provided with samples to lab; storage until end of study unless donor agrees to future use; nominal reimbursement provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimization of risk and confidentiality safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Study considered minimal risk; primary risks are breach of confidentiality and personal embarrassment from sample provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protections: deidentification, limited PHI collected (race/ethnicity only for reporting), secure locked storage of records, limited access to identifiers, informed consent process, and following RSRB requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: RSRB/IRB compliance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The study must be conducted in compliance with the approved protocol and RSRB determinations; consent forms bearing current RSRB watermark must be used; only most recently approved versions of consent and recruitment documents permitted; recruitment materials must be pre-approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI responsibilities include timely submission of continuing review reports (at least 8 weeks before expiration), requesting approval for changes, maintaining approved study documents, retaining signed consent forms ≥3 years, reporting unexpected serious problems, and submitting final progress reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety level and training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recombinant DNA and Lactobacillus handled at BSL1; infectious HIV-1 experiments performed under BSL2 containment with BSL3 practices (BSL2+); human biological fluids and primary cells handled under universal precautions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All personnel must undergo hands-on training before handling infectious virus; laboratories must be registered with and inspected by the Institutional Biosafety Committee; HBV vaccine offered to personnel handling primary human cells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animal use justification and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Animals (rabbits) will be used in R33 for the RVI assay only; justification: FDA guidance stipulates rabbit vaginal irritation assay as gold standard for topical microbicide tolerability; use of 27 rabbits (n=6 per group except N9 n=3) with specified dosing groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide justification for species and numbers; use standard small group sizes; if high variability observed, consult biostatistician to re-evaluate sample size. Animal care provided by AAALAC-accredited facility, with certified veterinarians and adherence to Animal Welfare Act and PHS policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures to limit animal discomfort
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures to ensure discomfort, distress, pain, and injury are limited to those unavoidable for scientifically sound research; use of sedation prior to vaginal administration of test agents where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed veterinary care, facility accreditation, and adherence to humane care policies are expected and described; investigators will follow approved protocols for minimizing pain and distress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milestone decision process with NIH program staff and consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Milestone decisions will be made following discussion with NIH Program Staff and with R21 phase consultants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed milestones guide go/no-go decisions and further development; interactions and reviews with program staff are part of the decision workflow.
